from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section2Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Mathematical Definition: The Eigen-Equation", [
            "Eigen-equation is Av equals lambda times v.",
            "Lambda represents the scaling factor of elongation.",
            "Det A minus lambda I equals zero."
        ])
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Display the matrix equation A * v = λ * v in white
        equation = MathTex("A", "v", "=", "\\lambda", "v")
        equation[0].set_color("#FFFF00") # A yellow
        equation[1].set_color("#00FF00") # v green
        equation[4].set_color("#00FF00") # v green
        self.place_at_grid(equation, 'B2', scale_factor=1.5)
        self.play(Write(equation))
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#FFFF00")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Lambda represents the scaling factor
        self.play(Indicate(equation[3]))
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#00FF00")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Det A minus lambda I equals zero
        det_eq = MathTex("\\text{det}(A - \\lambda I) = 0")
        self.place_at_grid(det_eq, 'D2', scale_factor=1.2)
        self.play(Write(det_eq))
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#ADD8E6")
        
        self.wait(2)

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Visualizing Eigenbasis", [
            "Eigenvectors can form a coordinate basis.",
            "The matrix becomes diagonal in this basis.",
            "Complex calculations simplify to independent scaling."
        ])
        
        # Define objects
        plane = Axes(x_range=[-3, 3], y_range=[-3, 3], axis_config={"include_tip": True}).scale(0.6)
        v1 = Vector([1, 1], color=WHITE)
        v2 = Vector([-1, 1], color=WHITE)
        
        group = VGroup(plane, v1, v2)
        self.place_in_area(group, 'A2', 'E5')
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(Create(plane), Create(v1), Create(v2))
        self.lecture[0].set_color(YELLOW)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Rotate vectors/plane transformation
        self.play(Rotate(group, angle=PI/6))
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[1].set_color(YELLOW)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Highlight vectors remaining on span (in this case, original eigenvectors would stretch)
        # Using red for highlighting as requested
        highlight_v1 = Vector([1, 1], color=RED).move_to(v1.get_center())
        highlight_v2 = Vector([-1, 1], color=RED).move_to(v2.get_center())
        self.play(FadeIn(highlight_v1), FadeIn(highlight_v2))
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[2].set_color(YELLOW)
        self.wait(2)

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Real-world Application: Vibration & Stability", [
            "Eigenvalues represent system vibration frequencies.",
            "Eigenvectors define the bridge's vibration shape.",
            "Resonance occurs at specific eigen-frequencies."
        ])
        
        # Animations
        # Define visual elements
        sine_wave = FunctionGraph(lambda x: 0.5 * np.sin(3 * x), x_range=[-2, 2], color=WHITE)
        bridge_shape = VGroup(
            Line(LEFT*2, RIGHT*2),
            CurvedArrow(LEFT*1.5+DOWN*0.5, RIGHT*1.5+DOWN*0.5, angle=-PI/4),
        ).set_color(BLUE)
        resonance_marker = Circle(radius=0.3, color=YELLOW)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.place_in_area(sine_wave, "A1", "C6", scale_factor=0.8)
        self.play(Create(sine_wave))
        self.lecture[0].set_color(YELLOW)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.place_in_area(bridge_shape, "D1", "F6", scale_factor=0.8)
        self.play(FadeIn(bridge_shape))
        self.lecture[1].set_color(BLUE)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.place_at_grid(resonance_marker, "B3", scale_factor=0.5)
        self.play(ShowPassingFlash(resonance_marker))
        self.lecture[2].set_color(GREEN)
        self.wait(2)

class Section5Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Summary & Quick Check", [
            "Eigenvectors stay fixed in direction.", 
            "Eigenvalues describe the scaling factor.", 
            "Eigenbasis simplifies complex linear transformations."
        ])

        self.wait(1)

outline.topic: Eigenvectors, Eigenvalues, and Eigenbasis: The Geometry of Linear Transformations

sections.title: Intuitive Hook: The 'Stretch' Concept
sections.content: Introduce linear transformation as a visual deformation of space. Explain that while most vectors change direction when a matrix is applied, 'Eigenvectors' are the special directions that stay fixed on their original span.
sections.example: Visualize a grid of rubber bands: Applying a matrix is like stretching the grid. Most arrows rotate, but an eigenvector remains pointing along the same line, just elongated or compressed.

sections.title: Mathematical Definition: The Eigen-Equation
sections.content: Define Av = λv. Explain that 'v' (eigenvector) is the direction, and 'λ' (eigenvalue) is the scaling factor. Emphasize that for a non-zero vector to exist, det(A - λI) must equal zero.
sections.example: If matrix A scales a vector v by 3, λ=3. The equation Av = 3v shows the output is just a scalar multiple of the input.

sections.title: Visualizing Eigenbasis
sections.content: Explain that if we have enough linearly independent eigenvectors, they form a 'basis' for the space. In this basis, the transformation matrix becomes a simple diagonal matrix, making complex calculations trivial.
sections.example: Imagine a 2D plane defined by two eigenvectors. Instead of using x and y coordinates, we describe the world using 'eigen-coordinates', where every movement is just an independent stretch along these two axes.

sections.title: Real-world Application: Vibration & Stability
sections.content: Connect the concept to physical systems. Eigenvalues represent natural frequencies of vibration, and eigenvectors represent the 'shape' of those vibrations.
sections.example: A suspension bridge: Eigenvectors represent the specific shapes the bridge can bend into, and eigenvalues represent the frequencies at which it might collapse due to resonance.

sections.title: Summary & Quick Check
sections.content: Recap: Eigenvectors = Directions that don't rotate; Eigenvalues = Scale factors; Eigenbasis = A simplified coordinate system.
sections.example: A quick visual quiz: Show a transformation animation and ask students to identify the direction that did not rotate (the eigenvector).
